Replay

Replay Claimball

5 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
The group and the claimWhat is preserved and what is pending

Run this Claimball port to predict only the local avatar and shared ball before the authority settles their state. Replay Speedball instead predicts the complete pitch. Other active avatars are removed from the prediction group; the authority continues to simulate everyone. Original Claimball/Speedball/Slopball remain runnable in their original directories.

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_claimball/play.sh
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_claimball/run.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_claimball/run.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_claimball/network_run.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_claimball/compete_run.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_claimball/fault_run.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_claimball/stall_run.sh

The default opens a session menu with Solo, Host, Join and Watch. For automatic separate windows, set RCB_ROLE=host and RCB_ROLE=client; server and observer also work. Port defaults to 49490. RCB_PLAYERS is the start threshold, RCB_GOALS the winning score, and RCB_TOKEN a deterministic test identity label. Normal native menu play persists its identity and name in a separate profile. Launchers use localhost. WASD moves, Space kicks, E spikes. RCB_BOT=striker drives a match; idle watches; spiker retains the optional two-command scenario. Fault controls are RCB_LATENCY/RCB_JITTER in milliseconds and RCB_LOSS/RCB_DUPLICATE in ten-thousandths. Native macOS is tested; the WASM fixture is a type-check, not browser multiplayer acceptance.

The group and the claim#

shared/pitch declares a Prediction_Group, the subset of world state a client simulates speculatively. Projection builds that subset from an authority frame: it retains the local player/ball and records timestamped remote players (outsiders) separately. Its validator rejects reintroduced remote simulation members. The ordinary gameplay step iterates the group's connected players. Outside avatars do not produce predicted contacts, matching the original's predict-self policy; remote touches arrive through authoritative correction. See the group contract.

Presentation—the displayed state and effects—draws remote players from observed authority frames. A local influence inside 38 pixels claims the ball. The claim stays active through fast flight, including when the ball leaves reach. Once untouched and below 0.6 units/tick, it fades back to observed presentation over 0.25 seconds. A fast ball that this player never influenced does not create a claim. Claim state is presentation-only.

A claimed predicted goal reset stays on the predicted timeline until the observed reset catches up, then releases. This explicit reset latch prevents blending a new kickoff back toward the old goal position. It is an intentional clarification of the original's claim/reset behavior. Score/winner presentation remains authoritative, while the complete score and reset state participate in replay.

What is preserved and what is pending#

Pitch geometry, movement/momentum, kick cadence/reach/power, dribble contact, rolling friction/cap/bounce, goals, kickoff hold, team/spawn correspondence, claim reach and release thresholds are ported. Geometry provenance is in assets.md. The common rules were copied from the new Speedball port into this separate project, so each game remains independently buildable.

As in Replay Speedball, spikes carry intent and use the issuing seat's current world position rather than supplied coordinates; two queued commands run on successive ticks. The HUD/team tint are initial replacements. Native session menus, names, chat, scoreboard, leave/rejoin, Play again and native save/resume now have automated acceptance. Initial native Room handoff/crash migration is tested. Party menus and browser RTC handoff/crash paths are now tested locally. Steam, broader contested scenarios and human visual review remain pending. This is an initial M6 slice, not full parity or a paired performance comparison.

The four-process gate runs authority, striker, idle player and true observer at 240 ms gameplay RTT. It checks one predicted avatar per player, local speculative kicks, matching score/reset, five-authority-kick agreement in the recorded match, claim retention during fast distant flight, and actual Godot-node agreement with the selected predicted/observed pose. The idle player's underlying ball prediction can still receive large corrections; those are hidden by its observed presentation. RCB_GROUP and RCB_METRICS expose both facts. The original gate uses an idle opponent. compete_run.sh adds a second active striker, stops bot controls at tick 1800, lets the ball settle, and checks agreement/effect reconciliation. It need not finish a match; winning three goals is not its time limit. fault_run.sh adds 0–20 ms receive jitter, 10% unreliable-packet loss and 10% duplication, with seed 42 per adapter. Reliable application traffic stays ordered and delivered; this does not model ENet's lower-level retransmission/congestion loop. The gate requires observed drops/duplicates and both players' authoritative kicks, claims and views.

RCB_CONTEST counts remote kick effects presented while a local claim was active. This demonstrates overlapping interactions, not proof that a claim was obsolete: the local player may already have made a newer predicted touch. Claims still release under the authored proximity/speed/reset policy. The tests do not establish subjective quality during takeovers. RCB_PROFILE reports replay wall time and conservative histogram percentile bounds.

stall_run.sh pauses the idle client's main thread for 800 ms while the match continues. It requires an ahead-snapshot catch-up, no full resync, and preservation of all kick effects and final gameplay state. This covers a short local stall, not a blackout longer than the retained history. RCB_RESYNC prints reasons and tick frontiers if a full resync becomes necessary.

The native UI receipts retain an intermittent fault failure: the observer resynchronized and missed four kick presentations, despite converged final state. Later instrumented runs do not establish its cause or resolve that failure. The same-epoch resync fix separately proves and fixes loss of already confirmed effects when Welcome replaced the journal. A faulted checkpoint-refresh run preserves all eleven kicks, and old/current native plus WASM trace comparisons isolate the lost output. The cause of the older Facts_Overflow remains unestablished.

Play again is a round-scoped command in the current session. It retains identities and chat while resetting match state. Content C3 includes the round and event scope; C1/C2 peers and archives remain explicitly incompatible. See the session guide for behavior and reproduction.

Native authority saves and fresh-process solo/host resume are described in the session guide. The default checkpoint path is user://claimball.replay, configurable with RCB_SAVE; the matching host profile is required to resume. tests/replay_claimball_save/run.sh verifies exact moving state, ownership/error handling, rejoin, continued commands and match restart.

Native coordinator-driven handoff and crash recovery now have a separate migration guide. A successor restores the complete authority world while clients continue to predict one avatar. The shared package is named claimball_pitch to coexist with Speedball's pitch in service programs; its import path and verified C3 wire/save contracts remain unchanged.

Party menus and browser play use the shared provisioned Room adapters. Configure RCB_ROOM_SERVICE (browser query room_service) to create or join an invited party. Native/browser profiles remain separate from Party credentials; observers keep seat zero and do not receive succession checkpoints. The service can persist complete C3 checkpoints, with publication before and after browser migration independently decoded. Local test success does not establish a deployed public service or resolve the retained first-run browser fencing failure.
